description: The booking creates a Passenger Name Record; that generates Secure Flight Passenger Data, sent to government screening before a boarding pass issues. Once vetting completes the identity is frozen; changing a surname means changing the vetted identity, which requires re-vetting that cannot happen in real time.
energy_note: Nobody at the airport can fix it. Not a supervisor. Nobody.

aspect: And eVisas are bound to the exact MRZ
description: Many electronic visas are cryptographically linked to the exact machine-readable zone of the passport, so a minor spelling deviation invalidates the authorisation outright.
energy_note: A visa invalidated by one letter.

aspect: The defensive practice is unusual diligence
description: Copy the spelling from the MRZ, use the same passport for every booking, eVisa, hotel and loyalty profile, and contact the airline before check-in rather than at the airport. This is knowledge most travellers never need.
energy_note: Expertise in a system that shouldn't need any.

description: Her married surname is hyphenated on the passport and unhyphenated in the airline's 30-character field. She has flown on it eleven times. On the twelfth, a different carrier's system reads it differently and the boarding pass does not issue.
energy_note: Eleven flights fine, and the twelfth is a hyphen.
